ar: وأما الإنجيل الذي بأيديهم فهم معترفون بأنه لم يكتبه المسيح - عليه السلام - ولا أملاه على من كتبه وإنما أملوه بعد رفع المسيح متى ويوحنا وكانا قد صحبا المسيح ولم يحفظه خلق كثير يبلغون عدد التواتر، ومرقس ولوقا وهما لم يريا المسيح - عليه السلام - وقد ذكر هؤلاء أنهم ذكروا بعض ما قاله المسيح وبعض أخباره وأنهم لم يستوعبوا ذكر أقواله وأفعاله

ref.chapter: [فصل: وقوع التبديل في ألفاظ التوراة والإنجيل وانقطاع سندهما]

edition_note: al-Jawab al-Sahih li-man baddala din al-Masih, 2nd ed. (1419/1999), Dar al-'Asima (Saudi Arabia), eds. 'Ali ibn Hasan, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Ibrahim, Hamdan ibn Muhammad (per OpenITI #META# header). Page/volume from OpenITI PageV markers in Shamela_0000170 text; verify against the printed edition before quoting.
ar_before: ومن الناس من يقول أنه لم يكن نبيا وأنها قوبلت بنسخة وجدت عتيقة. وقد قيل أنه أحضرت نسخة كانت بالمغرب وهذا كله لا يوجب تواتر جميع ألفاظها ولا يمنع وقوع الغلط في بعضها ; كما يجري مثل ذلك في الكتب التي يلي نسخها ومقابلتها وحفظها القليل الاثنان والثلاثة.
ar_after: . ونقل اثنين وثلاثة وأربعة يجوز عليه الغلط لا سيما وقد غلطوا في المسيح نفسه حتى اشتبه عليهم بالمصلوب، ولكن النصارى يزعمون أن الحواريين رسل الله مثل عيسى ابن مريم وموسى - عليهما السلام - وأنهم معصومون وأنهم سلموا إليهم التوراة والإنجيل وأن لهم معجزات
gloss_en: As for the Gospel in their hands: they admit that Christ neither wrote it nor dictated it to its writers; rather Matthew and John, who had accompanied Christ, dictated it after Christ was raised. A large number of people reaching the level of tawatur did not memorise it. Mark and Luke, who had not seen Christ, [wrote it]; and these [writers] themselves state that they related some of what Christ said and some of his reports, and that they did not record all of his sayings and deeds. (Translation mine; 'أملوه' read as 'dictated'.)
what_it_says: Ibn Taymiyya says the Christian Gospels were not written or dictated by Christ, were compiled after the ascension (Matthew and John companions; Mark and Luke not eyewitnesses), were not memorised by a tawatur-sized group, and that the writers themselves admit they did not record everything.
why_relevant: Core statement of his claim that the Gospels fail the tawatur test; compare with the Torah passage T6-11, where he grants more reliability.
limits: He presents this as the position of 'the majority' argument for alteration (vol 2 p. 396), which he endorses in the following text. 'They admit' is his attribution; no Christian source is quoted here. The Gospels are anonymous in their bodies apart from Luke 1:1-4 and John 21:24, so the authorial attributions are from tradition, not from the passage.
attributed_to_christians: As Ibn Taymiyya presents it: Christians admit that Christ wrote or dictated none of the Gospels; Matthew and John (who accompanied Christ) wrote after the ascension; Mark and Luke did not see Christ; the books were not memorised by a large group.
christian_check: Mark not an eyewitness: Eusebius, Church History 3.39.15 (quoting 'the presbyter John' via Papias): Mark, 'having become the interpreter of Peter ... For he neither heard the Lord nor followed him' - https://www.newadvent.org/fathers/250103.htm (matches Ibn Taymiyya's claim about Mark). Luke's own preface (Luke 1:1-2, KJV): 'Forasmuch as many have taken in hand to set forth in order a declaration ... Even as they delivered them unto us, which from the beginning were eyewitnesses' - https://bible-api.com/luke+1:1-4?translation=kjv (Luke does not claim to have seen Christ; he claims to rely on eyewitness sources and on earlier written accounts). John 21:24 claims eyewitness authorship for the disciple - https://bible-api.com/john+21:24?translation=kjv
verdict_reason: Accurate on Mark's non-eyewitness status (Papias/Eusebius and Luke's own wording) and on the 'many things not recorded' point. Overstated where it presents the attributions and the 'they admit' framing as settled Christian positions: the texts do not name their authors, Luke's preface claims eyewitness sources and earlier accounts, and John 21:24 claims an eyewitness.

ar: وأما الأناجيل التي بأيدي النصارى: فهي أربعة أناجيل إنجيل متى ويوحنا ولوقا ومرقس وهم متفقون على أن لوقا ومرقس لم يريا المسيح، وإنما رآه متى ويوحنا، وأن هذه المقالات الأربعة التي يسمونها الإنجيل، وقد يسمون كل واحد منهم إنجيلا، إنما كتبها هؤلاء بعد أن رفع المسيح، فلم يذكروا فيها أنها كلام الله، ولا أن المسيح، بلغها عن الله، بل نقلوا فيها أشياء من كلام المسيح، وأشياء من أفعاله ومعجزاته. وذكروا أنهم لم ينقلوا كل ما سمعوه منه ورأوه
edition_note: al-Jawab al-Sahih li-man baddala din al-Masih, 2nd ed. (1419/1999), Dar al-'Asima (Saudi Arabia), eds. 'Ali ibn Hasan, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Ibrahim, Hamdan ibn Muhammad (per OpenITI #META# header). Page/volume from OpenITI PageV markers in Shamela_0000170 text; verify against the printed edition before quoting.
ar_before: ه مبلغ له عن الله وهو كلام الله لا كلامه. وفي القرآن - ما يبين أنه كلام الله - نصوص كثيرة وكان الذين رأوا محمدا - صلى الله عليه وسلم - ونقلوا ما عاينوه من معجزاته وأفعاله وشريعته وما سمعوه من القرآن وحديثه ألوفا مؤلفة أكثر من مائة ألف رأوه وآمنوا به.
ar_after: فكانت من جنس ما يرويه أهل الحديث والسير والمغازي عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - من أقواله وأفعاله التي ليست قرآنا. فالأناجيل التي بأيديهم شبه كتاب السيرة وكتب الحديث أو مثل هذه الكتب وإن كان غالبها صحيحا. وما قاله - عليه السلام - فهو مبلغ له عن الله
gloss_en: The Gospels in the hands of the Christians are four: the Gospels of Matthew, John, Luke and Mark. They agree that Luke and Mark did not see Christ and that only Matthew and John saw him; these four writings, which they call the Gospel (each of them may be called a Gospel), were written by them after Christ was raised. They did not state that these were God's words, nor that Christ conveyed them from God; rather they relate some of Christ's sayings, deeds and miracles. They themselves state that they did not relate everything they heard from him and saw. (Translation mine.)
what_it_says: Ibn Taymiyya's summary of the Christian Gospel base: four books, Mark and Luke not eyewitnesses, written after the ascension, not presented as God's speech, and by their own admission incomplete.
why_relevant: Gives the source base the tawatur argument is applied to (four books, few authors); the 'not everything recorded' admission is used as a key limit.
limits: 'وهم متفقون' ('they agree') is his claim of Christian consensus, not a quotation; the 'written after the ascension' and 'not God's words' points are his reading of the texts. Passage sits in the section on Christian arguments (vol 3 pp. 20-21).
attributed_to_christians: Christians (as summarised): four Gospels; Matthew and John saw Christ, Mark and Luke did not; the books were written after the ascension, are not presented as God's words, and do not record everything Christ said and did.
christian_check: Eusebius 3.39.15 (Mark, see above) matches the Mark point. 'Not everything recorded': John 20:30 (KJV) 'And many other signs truly did Jesus in the presence of his disciples, which are not written in this book' - https://bible-api.com/john+20:30-31?translation=kjv; John 21:25 'there are also many other things which Jesus did' - https://bible-api.com/john+21:25?translation=kjv. Luke 1:1-2 (see T6-01) says 'many have taken in hand' earlier accounts. The Gospels do not name their authors in the body of the text (John 21:24 is the only self-attribution, to 'the disciple').
verdict_reason: The 'not everything recorded' point and the Mark point are accurately reported. 'They agree' and the traditional eyewitness attribution to Matthew and John are his framing: the texts themselves do not name Matthew or Mark, and John 21:24 is an unnamed 'disciple' attribution, so the Matthew/John 'eyewitness' split is tradition, not stated in the texts.

ar: الوجه الرابع: أن التوراة والنبوات التي نقلت من نسخ اليهود والأناجيل هي أربعة كتب بعد المسيح عليه السلام، اثنان ممن كتبها لم يريا المسيح، وهما لوقا، ومرقس، واثنان رأياه، وهما يوحنا، ومتى. والنسخ إنما كثرت عن الأربعة، وما ينقله الأربعة لا يجب أن يكون متواترا معلوما

ref.chapter: [فصل: الرد عليهم في قولهم ومثل هذا القول في كتب الله المنزلة على أفواه الأنبياء والرسل شيء كثير]

edition_note: al-Jawab al-Sahih li-man baddala din al-Masih, 2nd ed. (1419/1999), Dar al-'Asima (Saudi Arabia), eds. 'Ali ibn Hasan, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Ibrahim, Hamdan ibn Muhammad (per OpenITI #META# header). Page/volume from OpenITI PageV markers in Shamela_0000170 text; verify against the printed edition before quoting.
ar_before: ة التي في زمن الحواريين أين هي؟ ومن رآها؟ ولو قدر أنها كانت بالعربية، فهذه النسخ اليوم العربية الموجودة بأيدي الناس هي مما عرب مما بأيديهم، وحينئذ فلا تعرف صحتها إن لم تعرف صحة الترجمة، ويثبت نقل تلك عن المسيح عليه السلام، وهكذا القول في سائر الألسن.
ar_after: ، وإذا كثرت الألسن بها فمن بعد الأربعة، لا أن الذين سمعوها من المسيح عليه السلام تكلموا باثنين وسبعين لسانا، فإن هذا لم يقله أحد، ولا يقوله عاقل، إذ الحواريون كانوا اثني عشر لم يكونوا اثنين وسبعين، فإذا قيل: إنه نقلها اثنان وسبعون، فهم نقلوها عمن نقل
gloss_en: Fourth point: the Torah and the prophetic books transmitted from the copies of the Jews, and the Gospels, are four books after Christ. Two of their writers did not see Christ, Luke and Mark; two saw him, John and Matthew. Copies multiplied from the four, and what the four transmit need not be known by tawatur. (Translation mine; the sentence on the Torah is brief and not argued here.)
what_it_says: Reply to the Christian claim that their books were transmitted identically from the apostles: the Gospel base is four authors (two eyewitness, two not), and copies multiplied only from those four, so their content is not established by tawatur.
why_relevant: Direct statement that the Gospel's content lacks tawatur; it is the reply to the quoted Christian claim in T6-08 and to the letter quoted from vol 3 p. 414.
limits: Reply section ('الوجه الرابع') within a long rebuttal of a quoted Christian letter (vol 3 pp. 414-425; the Christian claim is quoted there). The sentence on the Torah is terse and its grammatical object is 'the Torah and prophetic books' transmitted from Jewish copies. 'لا يجب أن يكون متواترا' = 'need not be tawatur' (his logical claim, not 'is not tawatur').
attributed_to_christians: Christians (in the quoted letter) hold that their Torah, prophetic books and Gospels were handed from the apostles in identical form; Ibn Taymiyya here assigns the Gospel base to four writers.
christian_check: Same sources as T6-01/T6-02: Luke 1:2 https://bible-api.com/luke+1:1-4?translation=kjv; John 21:24 https://bible-api.com/john+21:24?translation=kjv; Eusebius 3.39.15 https://www.newadvent.org/fathers/250103.htm (Mark not a hearer of the Lord).
verdict_reason: Correctly identifies the four canonical Gospels and the status of Mark and Luke, but the strong inference that the content therefore lacks tawatur is his judgement; the Christian sources in view (Luke 1:1-4) claim multiple earlier accounts and eyewitness testimony, which he does not address here.

ar: فالمسلمون عندهم من الأخبار عن نبيهم ما هو متواتر وما اتفقت الأمة المعصومة على تصديقه، وما قامت دلائل صدقه من غير هذه الجهة مثل: أن يخبر واحد أو اثنان أو ثلاثة بحضرة جمع كثير لا يجوز أن يتواطئوا على الكذب بخبر يقولون إن أولئك عاينوه وشاهدوه فيقرونهم على هذا ولا يكذب به منهم أحد فيعلم بالعادة المطردة أنه لو كان كاذبا لامتنع اتفاق أهل التواتر على السكوت عن تكذيبه كما يمتنع اتفاقهم على تعمد الكذب. وإذا نقل الواحد والاثنان ما توجب العادة اشتهاره وظهوره ولم يظهر، ونقلوه مستخفين بنقله لم ينقلوه على رءوس الجمهور، علم أنهم كذبوا فيه
edition_note: al-Jawab al-Sahih li-man baddala din al-Masih, 2nd ed. (1419/1999), Dar al-'Asima (Saudi Arabia), eds. 'Ali ibn Hasan, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Ibrahim, Hamdan ibn Muhammad (per OpenITI #META# header). Page/volume from OpenITI PageV markers in Shamela_0000170 text; verify against the printed edition before quoting.
ar_before: م يغلط، وإن كان خبره لو تجرد عن تلك الدلائل أمكن كذبه أو غلطه كما أن الخبر المجرد لا يجزم بكذبه إلا بدليل يدل على ذلك إما قيام دليل عقلي قاطع أو سمعي قاطع على أنه بخلاف مخبره فيجزم ببطلان خبره وحينئذ فالمخبر إما كاذبا أو غالطا، وقد يعلم أحدهما بدليل.
ar_after: . ودلائل صدق المخبر وكذبه كثيرة متنوعة ليس هذا موضع بسطها، ولكن المقصود هنا أن المسلمين تواتر عندهم عن نبيهم ألفاظ القرآن ومعانيه المجمع عليها والسنة المتواترة وعندهم عن نبيهم أخبار كثيرة معلومة الصدق بطرق متنوعة كتصديق الأمة المعصومة ودلالة العادات
gloss_en: Muslims have among the reports from their Prophet what is mutawatir, what the infallible community agreed to accept, and what is shown true by other evidence. Example: if one, two or three people report, in the presence of a large crowd that could not conspire to lie, an event they say those [present] witnessed, and no one in the crowd denies it, then it is known from constant custom that had they been lying the mutawatir [witnesses] would not have kept silent, just as they could not agree to lie deliberately. And if one or two transmit what custom requires to be widely known and visible, and it was not, and they transmitted it secretly and not in front of the public, they lied in it. (Translation mine.)
what_it_says: States his general epistemic test: tawatur, consensus of the infallible community, and surrounding evidence; a single report made before a large unchallenged crowd can be accepted; a report of a public event by one or two people that was not widely known is a sign of lying.
why_relevant: Gives the general criterion he uses against Christian and Jewish reports (including the crucifixion), with a built-in test for public events; a useful consistency check.
limits: The criteria are stated for Islamic reports (hadith and Quran). Whether the 'large crowd unchallenged' test applies to the crucifixion account is not stated here; he applies it elsewhere (T6-06/07). Arabic 'فيعلم بالعادة المطردة' = 'known by consistent habit'.

ar: وهم يحفظون القرآن في صدورهم لا يحتاجون في حفظه إلى كتاب مسطور، فلو عدمت المصاحف من الأرض لم يقدح ذلك فيما حفظوه. بخلاف أهل الكتاب فإنه لو عدمت نسخ الكتب لم يكن عندهم به نقل متواتر بألفاظها إذ لا يحفظها - إن حفظها - إلا قليل لا يوثق بحفظهم فلهذا كان أهل الكتاب بعد انقطاع النبوة عنهم يقع فيهم من تبديل الكتب إما تبديل بعض أحكامها ومعانيها، وإما تبديل بعض ألفاظها ما لم يقوموا بتقويمه. ولهذا لا يوجد فيهم الإسناد الذي للمسلمين
edition_note: al-Jawab al-Sahih li-man baddala din al-Masih, 2nd ed. (1419/1999), Dar al-'Asima (Saudi Arabia), eds. 'Ali ibn Hasan, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Ibrahim, Hamdan ibn Muhammad (per OpenITI #META# header). Page/volume from OpenITI PageV markers in Shamela_0000170 text; verify against the printed edition before quoting.
ar_before: صدق المخبر وكذبه كثيرة متنوعة ليس هذا موضع بسطها، ولكن المقصود هنا أن المسلمين تواتر عندهم عن نبيهم ألفاظ القرآن ومعانيه المجمع عليها والسنة المتواترة وعندهم عن نبيهم أخبار كثيرة معلومة الصدق بطرق متنوعة كتصديق الأمة المعصومة ودلالة العادات وغير ذلك
ar_after: ، ولا لهم كلام في نقلة العلم وتعديلهم وجرحهم ومعرفة أحوال نقلة العلم ما للمسلمين ولا قام دليل سمعي ولا عقلي على أنهم لا يجتمعون على خطأ، بل قد علم أنهم اجتمعوا على الخطأ لما كذبوا المسيح. ثم كذبوا محمدا - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فإذا كانت الكتب المنقولة
gloss_en: They [the Muslims] memorise the Qur'an in their hearts and do not need a written book to memorise it; so if all the codices disappeared from the earth, this would not harm what they have memorised. Unlike the People of the Book: if the copies of their books were lost they would have no tawatur transmission of their wording, since few, if any, memorise them, and those few are not trusted in their memory. That is why, after prophecy ceased among them, alteration occurred in their books, of their meanings and of some of their wording. That is why they have no isnad like the Muslims'. (Translation mine.)
what_it_says: Contrasts Muslim transmission of the Qur'an (memorised by many, tawatur of wording, independent of codices) with the Christian and Jewish books (no tawatur of wording, few memorisers, copies only, alteration, no isnad system).
why_relevant: Central statement of why he thinks the Quran passes the tawatur test and the Christian books do not; also his claim about the absence of isnad among Christians.
limits: General assertions without counts for Christian memorisers; 'إلا قليل لا يوثق بحفظهم' (a few, whose memory is not trusted) is unsourced. The sentence before it (vol 3 p. 21) claims that over 100,000 people saw the Prophet; that figure is not sourced in the text. The 'isnad' claim is about Christian practice, and the passage does not describe the Christian chains of authority.
attributed_to_christians: Ibn Taymiyya says Christians rely on written copies and have no tawatur of their wording and no isnad-type science of transmitter criticism (ilm al-rijal).
christian_check: Eusebius 3.39.4 (Papias): Papias says he questioned those who had followed 'the elders' about 'the words of the elders', because 'I did not think that what was to be gotten from the books would profit me as much as what came from the living and abiding voice' - https://www.newadvent.org/fathers/250103.htm (so Christians did name chains of authorities for their traditions). Eusebius 3.39.15 names 'the presbyter John' as source for Mark. Luke 1:2 https://bible-api.com/luke+1:1-4?translation=kjv
verdict_reason: Accurate that the Christian books were not transmitted by a memorised tawatur of wording and that Christians lack a hadith-style isnad for each saying. Overstated as 'no isnad': early Christian writers (Papias, via Eusebius) named chains of oral and written authorities, and the 'few memorisers' claim is not quantified.

ar: ولم يكن في الأربعة من شهد صلب المسيح ولا من الحواريين بل ولا في أتباعه من شهد صلبه وإنما الذين شهدوا الصلب طائفة من اليهود فمن الناس من يقول أنهم: علموا أن المصلوب غيره وتعمدوا الكذب في أنهم صلبوه وشبه صلبه على من أخبروهم وهذا قول طائفة من أهل الكلام المعتزلة وغيرهم وهو قول ابن حزم وغيره

ref.chapter: [فصل: قيام الحجة على من بلغته دعوة الرسل]

edition_note: al-Jawab al-Sahih li-man baddala din al-Masih, 2nd ed. (1419/1999), Dar al-'Asima (Saudi Arabia), eds. 'Ali ibn Hasan, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Ibrahim, Hamdan ibn Muhammad (per OpenITI #META# header). Page/volume from OpenITI PageV markers in Shamela_0000170 text; verify against the printed edition before quoting.
ar_before: هم كانوا يعتقدون أن المسيح نفسه صلب كانوا مخطئين في ذلك ولم يكن هذا الخطأ مما يقدح في إيمانهم بالمسيح إذا آمنوا بما جاء به ولا يوجب لهم النار، فإن الأناجيل التي بأيدي أهل الكتاب فيها ذكر صلب المسيح وعندهم أنها مأخوذة عن الأربعة مرقس ولوقا ويوحنا ومتى
ar_after: ومنهم من يقول بل اشتبه على الذين صلبوه وهذا قول أكثر الناس، والأولون يقولون أن قوله: {وما قتلوه وما صلبوه ولكن شبه لهم} [النساء: 157] أي شبه للناس الذين أخبرهم أولئك بصلبه. الجمهور يقولون: بل شبه للذين يقولون صلبوه كما قد ذكرت القصة في غير هذا الموضع
gloss_en: None of the four [Gospel writers] witnessed the crucifixion of Christ, nor did any of the disciples or followers; rather, those who witnessed the crucifixion were a group of Jews. Some say that they knew the crucified one was someone else and deliberately lied that they had crucified him, and that his likeness was placed on the one they described; this is the view of some of the kalam people (Mu'tazila) and others, and of Ibn Hazm and others. (Translation mine.)
what_it_says: States that none of the four Gospel writers, nor any disciple, witnessed the crucifixion; only Jews did. He then lists the two positions (deliberate lie vs. confusion) and says the second is the view of most people.
why_relevant: Direct application of the witness test to the crucifixion: the claimed witnesses are Jews, not the Gospel authors.
limits: He lists views ('some say', 'most say') and does not state his own preferred explanation in this passage; the passage is inside an argument about the culpability of those who did not accept the messengers (vol 2 p. 302), not a historical treatise. 'ولم يكن في الأربعة من شهد' is an unqualified historical claim, which John's Gospel contradicts (see check).
attributed_to_christians: The Gospels contain the crucifixion; per Ibn Taymiyya, none of the four Gospel writers nor any disciple or follower saw it; the witnesses were Jews.
christian_check: John's Gospel places a disciple at the cross: John 19:25-27 (KJV) 'Now there stood by the cross of Jesus his mother ... When Jesus therefore saw his mother, and the disciple standing by, whom he loved' - https://bible-api.com/john+19:25-27?translation=kjv; John 19:35 'And he that saw it bare record, and his record is true' - https://bible-api.com/john+19:35?translation=kjv. Mark 14:50 'And they all forsook him, and fled.' - https://bible-api.com/mark+14:50?translation=kjv (matches the flight of disciples). Mark 15:40-41 'There were also women looking on afar off' - https://bible-api.com/mark+15:40-41?translation=kjv; Luke 23:49 'all his acquaintance, and the women ... stood afar off' - https://bible-api.com/luke+23:49?translation=kjv
verdict_reason: Right about Mark and Luke, where the disciples flee and women and acquaintances watch from afar. Misses John's text, which places the beloved disciple at the cross and claims an eyewitness record (19:26, 19:35), so 'none of the four witnessed' does not match the Gospel of John as written.

ar: ولم يكن أحد من النصارى شاهدا هذا معهم، بل كان الحواريون خائفين غائبين، فلم يشهد أحد منهم الصلب، وإنما شهده اليهود وهم الذين أخبروا الناس أنهم صلبوا المسيح، والذين نقلوا أن المسيح صلب من النصارى وغيرهم، إنما نقلوه عن أولئك اليهود وهم شرط من أعوان الظلمة، لم يكونوا خلقا كثيرا يمتنع تواطؤهم على الكذب.

ref.chapter: [فصل: نقض دعواهم أن القرآن أثبت في المسيح اللاهوت والناسوت]

edition_note: al-Jawab al-Sahih li-man baddala din al-Masih, 2nd ed. (1419/1999), Dar al-'Asima (Saudi Arabia), eds. 'Ali ibn Hasan, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Ibrahim, Hamdan ibn Muhammad (per OpenITI #META# header). Page/volume from OpenITI PageV markers in Shamela_0000170 text; verify against the printed edition before quoting.
ar_before: موا أنها بغي، ومنها: قولهم: {إنا قتلنا المسيح عيسى ابن مريم رسول الله} [النساء: 157] . قال تعالى: {وما قتلوه وما صلبوه ولكن شبه لهم} [النساء: 157] . وأضاف هذا القول إليهم وذمهم عليه. ولم يذكر النصارى ; لأن الذين تولوا صلب المصلوب المشبه به هم اليهود،
ar_after: قال تعالى: {وما قتلوه وما صلبوه ولكن شبه لهم} [النساء: 157] . فنفى عنه القتل، ثم قال: {وإن من أهل الكتاب إلا ليؤمنن به قبل موته} [النساء: 159] . وهذا عند أكثر العلماء معناه قبل موت المسيح، وقد قيل قبل موت اليهودي وهو ضعيف، كما قيل: أنه قبل موت محمد ص
gloss_en: The Christians are not mentioned [in Q 4:157] because those who undertook the crucifixion of the crucified one (the one resembling him) were the Jews; no Christian was present with them; rather the disciples were frightened and absent, so none of them witnessed the crucifixion. Only the Jews witnessed it, and they told people that they had crucified the Messiah. The Christians and others who relate that Christ was crucified relate it only from those Jews, who were agents ('shurat') of the oppressors, and were not a numerous group whose agreement to lie would be impossible. (Translation mine.)
what_it_says: Argues that the crucifixion account reaches Christians only through a small group of Jewish witnesses, who could be lying; he uses this to explain the Quranic verse 4:157 and to deny that the Christian account is mutawatir.
why_relevant: Clearest explicit application of the tawatur criterion to the crucifixion. Compare with his public-event test (T6-04).
limits: 'شرط من أعوان الظلمة' is rendered as 'agents (shurat) of the oppressors' (shurta = police/guards); this is interpretive. The number of Jewish witnesses is not given. The claim that Christians received the account only from Jews is his inference. The passage is part of a commentary on Q 4:155-161.
attributed_to_christians: Christians (and others) say Christ was crucified; per Ibn Taymiyya their report derives from the Jews who were present, and no Christian was present; the disciples were frightened and absent.
christian_check: The Gospels do not say the crucifixion report came from Jews: Mark 15:40-41 (women watching; https://bible-api.com/mark+15:40-41?translation=kjv), John 19:25-27 and 19:35 (a disciple and an eyewitness record; https://bible-api.com/john+19:25-27?translation=kjv; https://bible-api.com/john+19:35?translation=kjv), Luke 23:49 (acquaintances and women; https://bible-api.com/luke+23:49?translation=kjv). Mark 14:50 supports the fear/flight claim (https://bible-api.com/mark+14:50?translation=kjv).
verdict_reason: Accurately reports Mark's flight of disciples and that the women and acquaintances watched from afar, which is the ground for his 'frightened and absent' claim. Misrepresents the Christian source claim: the Gospels present their crucifixion account as coming from women and (in John) a disciple who witnessed it, not from Jewish informants, and John 19 contradicts 'no disciple was present'.

ar: وأما قولهم كيف يمكن تغيير كتبنا التي هي مكتوبة باثنين وسبعين لسانا وفي كل لسان منها كذا وكذا ألف مصحف ومضى عليها إلى مجيء محمد أكثر من ستمائة سنة؟

ref.chapter: [فصل: الرد على قولهم كيف يمكن تغيير كتبنا التي هي مكتوبة باثنين وسبعين لسانا]

edition_note: al-Jawab al-Sahih li-man baddala din al-Masih, 2nd ed. (1419/1999), Dar al-'Asima (Saudi Arabia), eds. 'Ali ibn Hasan, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Ibrahim, Hamdan ibn Muhammad (per OpenITI #META# header). Page/volume from OpenITI PageV markers in Shamela_0000170 text; verify against the printed edition before quoting.
ar_before: د من الأنبياء ولا عن الحواريين وهم يجوزون لأكابر أهل العلم والدين أن يغيروا ما رأوه من الشرائع ويضعوا شرعا جديدا فلهذا كان أكثر شرعهم مبتدعا لم ينزل به كتاب ولا شرعه نبي. | [فصل: الرد على قولهم كيف يمكن تغيير كتبنا التي هي مكتوبة باثنين وسبعين لسانا]
ar_after: فيقال: أما بعد انتشارها هذا الانتشار فلم يقل المسلمون، بل ولا طائفة معروفة منهم إن ألفاظ جميع كل نسخة في العالم غيرت لكن جمهور المسلمين الذين يقولون إن في ألفاظها ما غير إنما يدعون تغيير بعض ألفاظها قبل المبعث، أو تغيير بعض النسخ بعد المبعث لا تغيير
gloss_en: Their saying: 'How can our books be changed, when they are written in seventy-two languages, with so many thousands of copies in each language, and when more than six hundred years passed over them until the time of Muhammad?' (Translation mine.)
what_it_says: Quotes the Christian objection, as he presents it verbatim, that their scriptures cannot have been altered because of their translations and copies.
why_relevant: Shows exactly which Christian argument he is answering; the '72 languages' claim is attributed to them here.
limits: Quotation of a Christian letter (attributed in vol 1 p. 100 to Paul the Monk, bishop of Sidon, of Antioch); Ibn Taymiyya says he quotes their words verbatim, chapter by chapter. I did not consult the letter itself, so the quotation is not independently checked. The surrounding passage (vol 3 p. 30) is his reply.
attributed_to_christians: Christians hold that their scriptures exist in seventy-two languages, with thousands of copies in each, and were not changed in the six centuries before Muhammad.
verdict_reason: The quotation's fidelity to the original Christian letter could not be checked here (the letter was not consulted). The claim about textual stability is a factual question that this check does not settle.

ar: معلوم باتفاق النصارى أن المسيح لم يكن يتكلم إلا بالعبرية كسائر أنبياء بني إسرائيل، وأنه كان مختونا ختن بعد السابع كما يختن بنو إسرائيل وأنه كان يصلي إلى قبلتهم لم يكن يصلي إلى الشرق ولا أمر بالصلاة إلى الشرق. ومن قال إن لسانه كان سريانيا كما يظنه بعض الناس فهو غالط فالكلام المنقول عنه في الأناجيل إنما تكلم به عبريا ثم ترجم من تلك اللغة إلى غيرها.

ref.chapter: [فصل: الرد على قولهم كيف يمكن تغيير كتبنا التي هي مكتوبة باثنين وسبعين لسانا]

edition_note: al-Jawab al-Sahih li-man baddala din al-Masih, 2nd ed. (1419/1999), Dar al-'Asima (Saudi Arabia), eds. 'Ali ibn Hasan, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Ibrahim, Hamdan ibn Muhammad (per OpenITI #META# header). Page/volume from OpenITI PageV markers in Shamela_0000170 text; verify against the printed edition before quoting.
ar_before: وا أن أحدا لا يمكنه ذلك. وأما من ذكر أن التغيير وقع في أول الأمر فهم يقولون إنما أخذت الأناجيل عن أربعة، اثنان منهم لم يريا المسيح، بل إنما رآه اثنان من نقلة الإنجيل متى ويوحنا. ومعلوم إمكان التغير في ذلك. وأما قولهم إنها مكتوبة باثنين وسبعين لسانا ف
ar_after: والترجمة يقع فيها الغلط كثيرا كما وجدنا في زماننا من يترجم التوراة من العبرية إلى العربية ويظهر في الترجمة من الغلط ما يشهد به الحذاق الصادقون ممن يعرف اللغتين. والنصارى يقولون إنما كتبت بأربع لغات: (بالعبرية والرومية واليونانية والسريانية) . وأما قو
gloss_en: It is known by the agreement of all Christians that the Messiah spoke only Hebrew, like the prophets of the Children of Israel, and that he was circumcised after the seventh day as the Children of Israel are, and that he prayed toward their qibla. Whoever says that his language was Syriac, as some people think, is mistaken; the words transmitted from him in the Gospels were spoken in Hebrew and then translated from that language into others. (Translation mine.)
what_it_says: States, as the consensus of all Christians, that Jesus spoke Hebrew only, that the Gospel words are translations from Hebrew, and that Syriac claims are mistaken.
why_relevant: A claim about Christian consensus on the language of the Gospel words, which the Gospel text can test. It also shows his reasoning about translation errors, which he uses against the Christian books.
limits: 'باتفاق النصارى' (by agreement of all Christians) is his assertion. The text does not discuss the Aramaic words in the Gospels. Circumcision and qibla claims are not checked here.
attributed_to_christians: All Christians agree that Jesus spoke only Hebrew, that the Gospel wording comes from Hebrew translated into other languages, and that claims of a Syriac original are mistaken.
christian_check: Gospel text contains non-Greek words given with translations: Mark 5:41 'Talitha cumi; which is, being interpreted, Damsel, I say unto thee, arise.' - https://bible-api.com/mark+5:41?translation=kjv; Mark 15:34 'Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani? which is, being interpreted, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?' - https://bible-api.com/mark+15:34?translation=kjv; Mark 7:34 'Ephphatha, that is, Be opened.' - https://bible-api.com/mark+7:34?translation=kjv. John 19:20 says the inscription was 'written in Hebrew, and Greek, and Latin' - https://bible-api.com/john+19:20?translation=kjv (the Gospel uses 'Hebrew' as the name of the local language, which supports his terminology).
verdict_reason: The universal-consensus claim is overstated, and the Gospel text transliterates non-Greek words that it glosses in translation. The Gospel of John calls the language 'Hebrew', so his terminology has textual support. Whether the language was Hebrew or Aramaic is a scholarly question I did not settle.

ar: فإن النقل عن محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم مدته قريبة، والناقلون عنه أضعاف أضعاف من نقل دين المسيح عنه، وأضعاف أضعاف أضعاف من اتصل به نقل دين موسى عليه السلام، فإن أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ما زالوا كثيرين منتشرين في مشارق الأرض ومغاربها، وما زال فيهم من هو ظاهر بالدين منصور على الأعداء، بخلاف بني إسرائيل، فإنهم زال ملكهم في أثناء الأمر لما خرب بيت المقدس الخراب الأول بعد داود عليه السلام ونقص عدد من نقل دينهم حتى قد قيل إنه لم يبق من يحفظ التوراة إلا واحد. والمسيح عليه السلام لم ينقل دينه عنه إلا عدد قليل

ref.chapter: [فصل: النصارى بدلوا دين المسيح قبل مبعث النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم]

edition_note: al-Jawab al-Sahih li-man baddala din al-Masih, 2nd ed. (1419/1999), Dar al-'Asima (Saudi Arabia), eds. 'Ali ibn Hasan, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Ibrahim, Hamdan ibn Muhammad (per OpenITI #META# header). Page/volume from OpenITI PageV markers in Shamela_0000170 text; verify against the printed edition before quoting.
ar_before: بالقرآن، أو شرع الصلوات الخمس، وصوم رمضان، وحج البيت الحرام؛ وجحد محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، وما تواتر عنه أعظم من جحد أتباع الحواريين المسيح عليه السلام، وإرساله لهم إلى الأمم، ومجيئه بالإنجيل، وجحد مجيء موسى عليه السلام بالتوراة، وجحد أنه كان يسبت ;
ar_after: لكن النصارى يزعمون أنهم رسل الله معصمون مثل: إبراهيم وموسى، وسيأتي الكلام على هذا إن شاء الله تعالى إذا وصلنا إليه، إذ المقصود هنا بيان من زعم أن محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقول: إنه لم يبعث إلا إلى مشركي العرب، فإنه في غاية الجهل والضلال أو غاية ا
gloss_en: The transmission from Muhammad is recent, and those who transmitted from him far exceed those who transmitted Christ's religion from him, and far exceed by much more those who transmitted the religion of Moses. The community of Muhammad has remained numerous and spread across East and West ... unlike the Children of Israel, whose rule ended when the first destruction of Jerusalem came after David, and whose number of transmitters decreased until it was said that none remained who memorised the Torah except one. Christ's religion was transmitted by him only by a small number. (Translation mine; 'قيل' = 'it was said'.)
what_it_says: Argues for the reliability of Muslim transmission by numbers: transmitters from Muhammad far exceed those for Christ and Moses; the Torah transmission is said to have been reduced to one memoriser; Christ's religion was transmitted by a small number.
why_relevant: Gives his comparative use of numbers to judge transmission and an explicit claim about the small number transmitting Christ's religion.
limits: The Torah memoriser claim is hedged ('حتى قد قيل'). 'عدد قليل' is not quantified. The passage is an argument for Muhammad's prophethood (vol 1 p. 369), not a historical study of the Christian community. The passage does not address Christian claims of larger early groups.
attributed_to_christians: No Christian statement is quoted here; in context he attributes to the Christians the claim that their apostles are infallible messengers who transmitted their religion. His claim is that Christ's religion was transmitted by a small number.
christian_check: Acts 1:15 (KJV) 'And in those days Peter stood up in the midst of the disciples, and said, (the number of names together were about an hundred and twenty,)' - https://bible-api.com/acts+1:15?translation=kjv; 1 Corinthians 15:6 (KJV) 'After that, he was seen of above five hundred brethren at once' - https://bible-api.com/1+corinthians+15:3-8?translation=kjv. The apostolic core is small (the Gospels and Acts name twelve), so 'a small number' is partly right, but the Christian texts report larger groups which the passage does not address.
verdict_reason: The core of twelve apostles is consistent with the Christian texts, but the Christian texts also report a group of about 120 (Acts 1:15) and more than 500 witnesses (1 Cor 15:6). Ibn Taymiyya does not mention these, so his 'small number' claim is incomplete as a description of the Christian sources.

ar: فالتوراة باتفاق الخلق مأخوذة عن موسى بن عمران وهو معصوم، وإنما يطعن من يطعن في نقل بعضها لانقطاع التواتر في أثناء المدة لما خرب بيت المقدس، ولم يبق فيه ساكن، أكثر من سبعين سنة، فيقول بعض الناس: إن بعض ألفاظها غير حينئذ، ويقول بعضهم: لم تغير ألفاظ جميع النسخ، وإنما غير ألفاظ بعض النسخ، وانتشرت النسخ المغيرة عند كثير من الناس حتى لا يعرفوا غيرها
edition_note: al-Jawab al-Sahih li-man baddala din al-Masih, 2nd ed. (1419/1999), Dar al-'Asima (Saudi Arabia), eds. 'Ali ibn Hasan, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Ibrahim, Hamdan ibn Muhammad (per OpenITI #META# header). Page/volume from OpenITI PageV markers in Shamela_0000170 text; verify against the printed edition before quoting.
ar_before: - لم يلتفت إليه لأنهم معصومون. كل هذا مبني على دعوى عصمتهم، وقد عرف فساده، وإذا قالت النصارى: نحن ننقلها عن الحواريين المعصومين، قالت اليهود: نحن ننقلها عن موسى المعصوم باتفاق أهل الملل، أو عن العارف المعصوم باتفاق اليهود والنصارى، وكثير من المسلمين،
ar_after: . ثم بنو إسرائيل لم يزل فيهم نبي بعد نبي حتى جاء المسيح، وبعد المسيح فلم يزالوا خلقا كثيرا لا يمكن تواطؤهم في مشارق الأرض ومغاربها على تغيير نسخ التوراة، بخلاف الإنجيل فإنه إنما نقله أربعة، ومن كتب التوراة والزبور والنبوات من أتباع المسيح، فإنما كتبو
gloss_en: The Torah is, by the agreement of all people, taken from Moses son of Imran, who is infallible. What is in dispute is the transmission of some of it, because the transmission (tawatur) was broken in the period when Jerusalem was in ruins and no one lived there for more than seventy years. Some people say parts of its wording changed; others say that not all copies changed, only some, and the altered copies spread among many people until they knew no other. (Translation mine.)
what_it_says: Says the Torah's origin with Moses is agreed, but its tawatur was broken during the long ruin of Jerusalem (Babylonian period), so some alteration of wording is alleged by some and denied (for all copies) by others.
why_relevant: His clearest admission that the Torah's transmission was interrupted (انقطاع التواتر); it is the basis for his comparative claim (later in the same chapter) that the Torah's wording is more reliable than the Gospels'.
limits: The passage presents two positions and does not state the final judgement; the comparison 'Torah more reliable than Gospel' comes in the text immediately after the excerpt (vol 3 p. 425). Elsewhere he attributes the Torah's restoration to Ezra and to a single manuscript (vol 2 p. 396). Nebuchadnezzar is not named in this excerpt.
attributed_to_christians: Christians (and Jews) hold that the Torah comes from Moses; per Ibn Taymiyya it is agreed by all, and its transmission was interrupted only in the destruction period.
verdict_reason: The claim is about the Hebrew scriptures, and I did not check the Christian or Jewish accounts of the Babylonian-period transmission (for example the Ezra tradition in apocryphal Christian books). The text itself is clear about the claim.

ar: بل وكثير من علماء المسلمين الأكابر لا يعلمون ما هو متواتر عند أهل الكتاب، بل وعند غيرهم من علماء المسلمين مثل خراب بيت المقدس مرتين، ومجيء بخت نصر إلى بيت المقدس

ref.chapter: [فصل: ست طرق كبرى للقطع بنبوة محمد عليه السلام]

edition_note: al-Jawab al-Sahih li-man baddala din al-Masih, 2nd ed. (1419/1999), Dar al-'Asima (Saudi Arabia), eds. 'Ali ibn Hasan, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Ibrahim, Hamdan ibn Muhammad (per OpenITI #META# header). Page/volume from OpenITI PageV markers in Shamela_0000170 text; verify against the printed edition before quoting.
ar_before: ه لما أنكر عليه طلب السير: تسكت وإلا سألتك قدام الناس: أيهما كانت قبل، بدر أو أحد فإني أعلم أنك لا تعلمه. مع أنه من المتواتر الذي لا يستريب فيه من له أدنى معرفة بالأخبار أن أحدا كانت بعد بدر، وفي بدر انتصر المسلمون على الكفار، ويوم أحد استظهر الكفار.
ar_after: ، والله سبحانه قد ذكر في القرآن المرتين فقال: {وقضينا إلى بني إسرائيل في الكتاب لتفسدن في الأرض مرتين ولتعلن علوا كبيرا} [الإسراء: 4] (4) {فإذا جاء وعد أولاهما بعثنا عليكم عبادا لنا أولي بأس شديد فجاسوا خلال الديار وكان وعدا مفعولا} [الإسراء: 5] (5)
gloss_en: Many leading Muslim scholars do not know what is mutawatir for the People of the Book, and likewise for other Muslim scholars, such as the destruction of Jerusalem twice and the coming of Nebuchadnezzar to Jerusalem. (Translation mine; the passage continues with the Quranic verses 17:4-7 on the two destructions and his claim that the mutawatir report is that Nebuchadnezzar came first.)
what_it_says: Uses 'mutawatir' for historical reports (the two destructions of Jerusalem, Nebuchadnezzar) held by Jews and Christians, in contrast to scriptural wording. He says many Muslim scholars do not know these mutawatir reports.
why_relevant: Consistency test: he uses the tawatur label for Jewish and Christian historical reports while denying tawatur to their scriptural wording.
limits: 'Mutawatir' here means widely transmitted historical reports, not the wording of scripture; the sense differs from T6-05/T6-11. The following text (vol 6 p. 337) states that Christians have mutawatir reports on their history that Muslims do not know; that continuation is not extracted here. Nebuchadnezzar's dating is contested.
attributed_to_christians: Christians (and Jews) possess mutawatir historical reports about their own history, kings and scholars, which many Muslims do not know (his claim).
verdict_reason: Historical claim about the breadth of Jewish and Christian historical reports, not checked. It matters for the consistency check because he accepts Christian/Jewish historical tawatur while denying it for their scriptures.

ar: وأما القراءة الشاذة الخارجة عن رسم المصحف العثماني، مثل قراءة ابن مسعود وأبي الدرداء (60) رضي الله عنهما: {والليل إذا يغشى، والنهار إذا تجلى، والذكر والأنثى} (61) كما قد ثبت ذلك في الصحيحين. ومثل قراءة عبد الله (62): {فصيام ثلاثة أيام متتابعات}. وكقراءته: {إن كانت إلا زقية واحدة} (63) ونحو ذلك، فهذه إذا ثبتت عن بعض الصحابة فهل يجوز أن يقرأ بها في الصلاة؟ [ذلك] (64) على قولين للعلماء - هما روايتان مشهورتان عن الإمام أحمد - وروايتان عن مالك (65): - إحداهما: يجوز ذلك، لأن الصحابة والتابعين كانوا يقرأون بهذه الحروف في الصلاة. - والثانية: لا يجوز ذلك، وهو قول أكثر العلماء؛ لأن هذه القراءات لم تثبت متواترة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

ref.chapter: [القراءات الشاذة الخارجة عن رسم المصحف] (OpenITI editorial heading)

ar_before: لم يعلم غيره؛ فليس له أن يعدل عما علمه إلى ما لم يعلم، وليس له أن ينكر على من علم ما لم يعلمه من ذلك، ولا أن يخالفه، كما قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لا تختلفوا، فإن من كان قبلكم اختلفوا فهلكوا» (59). | CHECK [القراءات الشاذة الخارجة عن رسم المصحف]
ar_after: . وإن ثبتت فإنها منسوخة بالعرضة الآخرة. فإنه قد ثبت في الصحاح عن عائشة وابن عباس رضي الله عنهم، «أن جبريل عليه السلام كان يعارض النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالقرآن في كل عام مرة، فلما كان العام الذي قبض فيه عارضه به مرتين» (66). والعرضة الآخرة هي قراءة
gloss_en: Irregular (shadhdh) readings outside the 'Uthmanic codex, such as those of Ibn Mas'ud and Abu al-Darda, if established from some Companions: may one recite them in prayer? There are two well-known reports from Ahmad and two from Malik. One: it is permitted, because the Companions and Successors recited these letters in prayer. Two: it is not permitted, the view of most scholars, because these readings were not established as mutawatir from the Prophet; and even if established, they were abrogated by the last recitation ('arda al-akhira). (Translation mine.)
what_it_says: Presents the two positions on praying with irregular readings. The second (most scholars) rests on the claim that these readings were not transmitted as mutawatir and were abrogated.
why_relevant: Shows the tawatur criterion he uses for readings: a reading not established by tawatur is not Quran for prayer purposes (this view), while readings established otherwise are allowed (T6-15).
limits: He reports both positions and does not endorse the second in this excerpt; his own verdict comes at the end of the fatwa (T6-15). OpenITI editorial 'CHECK' tags and manuscript folio marks appear nearby, not inside this passage. The same wording is in Majmu' al-Fatawa vol. 13 p. 394.
duplicate_in_MajmucFatawa: Majmu' al-Fatawa vol. 13 p. 394 (same wording; Shamela text)

ar: لا نزاع بين العلماء المعتبرين بأن الأحرف السبعة التي ذكر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن القرآن أنزل عليها - ليست هي قراءات القراء السبعة المشهورة

ar_before: 18). فأما ذكر أقاويل الناس وأدلتهم وتقرير الحق فيها مبسوطا؛ فيحتاج من ذكر الأحاديث الواردة في ذلك وذكر ألفاظها وسائر الأدلة - إلى ما لا يتسع له هذا المكان. . ولا يليق بمثل هذا الجواب، ولكن نذكر النكت الجامعة التي تنبه على المقصود بالجواب، فنقول: (19)
ar_after: ، بل أول من جمع قراءات هؤلاء هو الإمام أبو بكر بن مجاهد (20) وكان على رأس المائة الثالثة ببغداد، فإنه أحب أن يجمع المشهور من قراءات: الحرمين والعراقين والشام، إذ هذه الأمصار الخمسة [هي] (21) التي خرج منها علم النبوة: من القرآن وتفسيره، والحديث (22)،
gloss_en: There is no dispute among the recognised scholars that the seven ahruf in which the Qur'an was revealed, as the Prophet said, are not the seven well-known readings of the seven readers. (Translation mine; the following text says Ibn Mujahid was the first to collect these readings, in the third century, for the five metropolitan centres.)
what_it_says: Says the seven ahruf of the Hadith are not the seven canonical readings (qira'at al-qurra' al-sab'a), which Ibn Mujahid collected in the third century.
why_relevant: His explicit statement on the seven ahruf (question d); it separates the Hadith's ahruf from the canonical readings.
limits: Only the first sentence is extracted; the rest explains that Ibn Mujahid chose seven to match the number of ahruf. The claim 'no dispute' is his. I did not find a verbatim parallel in Majmu' al-Fatawa vol. 13 (its wording differs), so cross-check if used.

ar_before: ه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى الناس، وبلغنا أصحابه عنه: الإيمان والقرآن حروفه ومعانيه، وذلك مما أوحاه الله إليه. كما قال تعالى: {وكذلك أوحينا إليك روحا من أمرنا ما كنت تدري ما الكتاب ولا الإيمان ولكن جعلناه نورا نهدي به من نشاء من عبادنا} (109).
ar_after: . والله أعلم بالصواب (110). تمت بحمد الله وعونه وحسن توفيقه في يوم الثلاثاء سادس عشرين جماد [ى] الأولى من شهور سنة تسع وخمسين وثمانمائة. (111)
gloss_en: Recitation in prayer and outside it is permitted with the established readings that agree with the consonantal text of the codex, as those readings were established; and they are then not irregular. (Translation mine.)
what_it_says: His conclusion: readings established (thabita) and matching the codex's consonantal text may be recited in and outside prayer, and are not irregular.
why_relevant: His verdict on the qira'at question. It uses 'established' (thabita), not 'mutawatir', as the criterion, which matters for the consistency check against T6-13 and against his statement in vol 20 p. 261 (not extracted).
limits: The text does not define 'established'. Majmu' al-Fatawa vol. 13 p. 402 has the same sentence; vol. 13 p. 400 says readings of al-A'mash, Ya'qub, Khalaf etc. are 'like the readings established of these seven for whomever they are established to'. The Risala's own marks show the source as Majallat al-Buhuth no. 13 (see edition note).
